To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the integrated human surveillance of WNV infections in Italy allowed to detect the circulation of the virus in 2012 and the implementation of preventive strategies to reduce the risk of transmission through blood components and organ transplant.
in 2012 in Italy 28 cases of WNND have been confirmed, 14 blood donors were positive for WNV and no solid organ donor was found to be positive for WNV.

1) in Italy, a West nile virus (WNV), neuroinvasive disease surveillance has been carried out each year since 2010 in the regions affected by the virus, 2) in 2012 the number of cases reported was higher than in previous years and 3) the surveillance system allowed the implementation of preventive strategies for WNV transmission by blood transfusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the epidemiology and the prevention of the WNV infection.

the development of new methods for the analysis of large data sets, and the application of these methods to problems in public health, with an emphasis on the analysis of infectious disease data, and on the development of new statistical methods to improve the surveillance and control of infectious diseases.
the development of an integrated human surveillance system for West Nile virus infections in Italy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Italian surveillance system for human WNV infection is a good example of a successful integrated “one health” approach.
the Italian experience in the surveillance of WNV infections in humans, animals and vectors is a successful model of integrated surveillance and prevention of emerging vector-borne diseases.
the Italian surveillance systems for WNV infections in humans have proved to be effective and useful in order to detect and prevent the spread of the disease in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Italian experience could represent a good example for other countries, where the WNV transmission is not yet established.

integrated surveillance of WNV infections in humans, animals and vectors is a key tool for the early detection of WNV circulation and for the prompt adoption of control measures to reduce the risk for human health.

the integrated human surveillance systems of WNV infections are a good example of the “one health” approach, and the results of the 2012 experience are a good example for future WNV surveillance activities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the implementation of integrated surveillance systems is a fundamental tool for an effective and efficient public health response to emerging diseases.

the integration of surveillance systems among human, animal, and vector control activities allows to obtain a more comprehensive and complete picture of the WNV circulation, which is fundamental for a more effective prevention and control of WNV infection.
integrated surveillance is a useful tool to monitor WNV circulation in Italy and that the integration of different surveillance systems is a good example of “one health” approach.
